quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing so other drivers can see you and your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: Only if you will ride longer than half an hour.

questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding. It protects you from the sun and dehydration in hot weather, and provides safety protection in all conditions.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Use hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let a tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume they have ridden on a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
Not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Always explain how to ride safely to your passenger. Never assume they already know what to do. Give complete instructions before every ride.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Bright, reflective clothing helps you be seen at any time. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright clothing during the day too.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if no other vehicles are approaching.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding on the shoulder.

questions.question: Keep an adequate distance between you and the vehicle ahead:

options.text: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
So traffic counters can count you as a vehicle.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to spot and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: A safe distance lets you stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also gives you a better view of road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield provides the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough protection.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to happen to:

options.text: Those who completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to beginning riders who are untrained and unfamiliar with their motorcycle.

questions.question: What is NOT required to get a motorcycle license?
questions.explanation: To get a motorcycle license, you need a vision test, a road sign reading test, a written test, and a riding skills test.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear is similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows down your motorcycle, just like using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Your body removes alcohol only through:
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Checking your mirrors:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful because you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal scanning. Also check them before you change lanes, stop at an intersection, or slow down.

questions.question: You should wear reflective clothing:
questions.explanation: Wear bright and reflective clothing anytime you ride. Crashes happen during the day and at night, so wear highly visible clothing at all times.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the bump better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact force. This helps prevent the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: When choosing footwear for riding, select:

options.text: Shoes with long laces that cannot be tucked in.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Use short heels so they do not catch on surfaces. Tuck in laces so they cannot catch on the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Be equally as effective as a face shield.
Offer the same protection as a windshield.
Provide protection for your entire face.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, the laces:

options.text: Should be removed from the shoes.

questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoe laces securely so they do not catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: The best lane position is one that:

options.text: Allows you to draft off other vehicles.
Allows other motorists to see you.
Places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows other motorists to see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should keep others from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears. Choose a position that gives you the most space.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce the chance of a crash?

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within one foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, other drivers must see you. Use your signals and brake light. Position yourself clearly in the lane. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What is downshifting also called?
questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it slows your motorcycle like braking does. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. How can you be more visible?
questions.explanation: Since most crashes occur during daylight, wear bright colors while riding. This helps other drivers see you, even in the day.

questions.question: Where should a motorcyclist position themselves in a lane?

options.text: Always stay in the same spot in the lane.
Weave between lane positions to keep other drivers out.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Do not worry about lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move to different positions in the lane as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What does smoothly downshifting allow a motorcyclist to do?
questions.explanation: Smoothly downshifting to engine brake is useful for motorcyclists. If you do this, also use your brake lights so other drivers know you are slowing down.
